name: mouse-lockon
note: 1.14.0: the mouse with the lock-on, among the two knights of room 5.12. Locked on, the game uses its lock-on camera with a view of its own, which the first build of the mouse turning the camera itself took for the play camera: the mouse moved then wrote its turn over the game's two camera pointers, and the game crashed (telemetry.cpp PlayCamera). Here the mouse is moved through a lock-on and after it, and the game plays on; and the mouse's wheel, a notch either way, changes the enemy locked on (keyboard.cpp MouseWheel: Change lock-on pressed), only with the mouse turning the camera. After them, in the open of the first courtyard, the mouse turns the play camera as far as before.

steps.until: room == 12 and player.active and not loading and not cutscene

steps.note: into the room: at its door a knight's blow knocks Hector out of it
both knights near: they walk up to Hector
the mouse not turning the camera: its wheel changes nothing
not locked on: the mouse turns the play camera itself (how far is the courtyard's to say: here a knight's blow can leave Hector in the room's corner, where the game's camera is held by its walls)
expect: found(runlog, r'mouse: turning the camera itself')

steps.note: the wheel with no lock-on: none taken
locked on, the mouse moved right and down: the game plays on (it crashed here), the lock-on kept
the wheel a notch up: the other knight
expect: found(runlog, 'mouse: the wheel changes the lock-on')

steps.note: and a notch down: changed again
the mouse again, on the other knight
let go: the play camera's again
and the mouse moved again: the game plays on
the first courtyard, in the open

steps.until: room == 1 and player.active and not loading and not cutscene

steps.note: after the lock-ons the mouse turns the play camera as before, 150 counts 18 degrees
